newsitem.title: CHINA: China marks "national shame" sites from Japan war.
newsitem.headline: China marks "national shame" sites from Japan war.

text.p: China's capital has marked eight sites of "national shame" to commemorate atrocities during Japan's occupation in the 1930s and 1940s, the official media said on Sunday.
A white marble stone was placed at each of the sites around the city and its suburbs where civilians or resistance fighters were killed by Japanese troops, the official Beijing Daily said.
One of the marker stones was placed in the Temple of Heaven, now a popular tourist attraction, said to have been used as the headquarters of a germ warfare unit.
Several hundred people attended a brief ceremony in Temple of Heaven Park on Saturday, it said.
Other markers were placed on what the official media said were sites of mass killings.
Japan occupied Manchuria in the northeast in 1931 and began an all-out invasion of China in 1937, events that still evoke strong emotions in China.
China estimates up to 31 million Chinese were killed or wounded by invading Japanese troops by the time the occupation ended with Japan's defeat in World War Two.
